text: Open-ground hint flip-flops while walking it: at (131,-84) 'about 220 to the north'; after following it 'about 250 to the south-east'; at (34,140) 'about 180 to the east', after walking 112 roughly that way 'about 210 to the west'. The hint is recomputed from where you stand, so the target jumps and distance grows; took ~2700 ticks (54 game s) and 6 F presses to find a legal site. Last two hints (60 W, 20 W) were accurate.

Nations panel (O) opened inside my settlement: the giant world-space settlement label '6 here, 7/20 residents' draws through the semi-transparent panel and collides with the Nations/Laws tabs at the top. Expected world labels hidden or dimmed behind full-screen panels.

Chronicle (opened with Y) shows 'Showing: > Your news' selected, yet the list is all other nations' raids and rivalries (e.g. 'Raiders from Westernport struck Westernland'); 259 entries, mostly raid spam. The only world-event news so far (tick 19751: 'A bountiful harvest came in across Castleburg...') is buried among ~50 raids, so a player would never notice nation world events happening.

Drought world event (tick 30551, first player event, ~611 game s in): sheet is clear - title, cause ('2 farms ... nothing for a day'), each option with cost and effect, 'The world waits while you decide'. Chose 1 'Dig irrigation ditches (15 wood, 10 stone)' while carrying only 5 stone: option was not greyed out, it went through, wood 44->29 and my stone 5->0; the other 5 stone was taken from somewhere (settlement store?) without saying so. Result toast and chronicle line are clear.

Drought option 3 'Ration and wait for rain' says 'your people grow restless with you', but the result toast/chronicle only says 'you rationed the stores and waited for rain.' No number or visible change: Player Info still reads 'Relationships: 0'. Code lowers every member's relationship with the player, but the player is never told by how much or where to see it. Also visible here: objective progress bar text clipped on the left ('mbers 7/10 . Buildings 2/2'), and 'Chronicle: your news' lists other nations' stalls.
